purpose: Covered unit-suite parallelism probe; preserve four isolated workers as the baseline and do not adopt the experimental shared-process partition
profile: Node 26.10.0, existing unit tier selection, TypeScript bootstrap, CPU test hook, Node LCOV reporter, /usr/bin/time user+system CPU
control: Previous direct covered sequential partition used about 233.05 CPU seconds and 65.14 wall seconds for the same test counts; the four-worker overlap saved about 23% wall time for about 3% more CPU. The fully isolated authoritative suite remains at four workers and previously measured 645.49 CPU seconds/139.99 wall seconds.
decision: Keep four isolated workers. The overlap is the best measured CPU/wall compromise but depends on the unadopted shared-process partition, whose coverage and home/module isolation differ. Raising isolated workers to six or eight adds 14% or 25% CPU for this partition, costly under concurrent missions.
